text:
Macklin Celebrini reached 200 NHL points in Pittsburgh this week, the fifth-youngest player in league history to get there, in a shootout loss that summed up San Jose's month: good night for the kid, no win for the team. He's 20, playing over 23 minutes a night, and has 23 points in 19 games for a club still waiting for help to arrive around him.

His last ten games have been quieter than they should be: 9 points against the 14 our numbers expected from his chances and ice time. He's shooting 10% against a talent range closer to 14%, so the goals are lagging, not the play. He has 79 shots, and the Sharks are a 10-point better five-on-five team by relative expected goals when he's out there.

The comparisons are already outrageous. Forwards picked in the top three since 2005 scored a median 0.55 points a game in their first full season; he's at 1.21 in his third. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 99th percentile among forwards in primary shot assists last season. What to watch: whether the finishing catches up while San Jose is still in games.
headline: The Sharks' rebuild has one finished piece
